edges.description: Accumulation of mutations and chromosomal alterations
The neuroendocrine/neuronal-like differentiation program enables SCLC cells to form functional synapses with neurons.
Synaptic input from neurons drives the pro-proliferative response of SCLC cells.
Neuronal synaptic transmission engages glutamatergic signaling that the tumor becomes dependent on.

nodes.description: SCLC cells can form functional synapses with neurons and receive synaptic transmission.

evidence.reference_title: Functional synapses between neurons and small cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: Here we show that SCLC cells can form functional synapses and receive synaptic transmission.

nodes.description: Loss of TP53 and RB1 leads to widespread genomic instability with frequent chromosomal gains and losses. Amplification of MYC family genes (MYC, MYCL, MYCN) occurs in ~20% of SCLC and is associated with worse prognosis.

evidence.snippet: Genomic profiling of SCLC reveals genetic instability

nodes.description: Inhibition of glutamate signaling has therapeutic efficacy in SCLC models, implicating glutamatergic signaling in tumor growth.

evidence.reference_title: Functional synapses between neurons and small cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: Moreover, inhibition of glutamate signalling had therapeutic efficacy in an autochthonous mouse model of SCLC.

nodes.description: Combined TP53 and RB1 loss eliminates major cell cycle checkpoints. Cells proliferate rapidly without the normal restraints on replication. This explains the rapid doubling time and initial chemosensitivity (dividing cells are vulnerable to chemotherapy).

evidence.snippet: their broad tumor suppressive functions are eliminated and a normal cell is able to proliferate indefinitely, escape entering into cellular senescence, and evade death

nodes.description: SCLC cells exhibit neuroendocrine differentiation, expressing markers such as synaptophysin, chromogranin A, and CD56 (NCAM). Neuroendocrine phenotype is regulated by lineage transcription factors (ASCL1, NEUROD1). Some SCLC produces paraneoplastic hormones (ACTH, ADH).
SCLC cells gain a proliferation advantage when co-cultured with neurons.

biological_processes: positive regulation of cell population proliferation

evidence.reference_title: Functional synapses between neurons and small cell lung cancer.
evidence.snippet: we showed that SCLC cells derive a proliferation advantage when co-cultured with vagal sensory or cortical neurons.

nodes.description: RB1 is inactivated in >90% of SCLC through mutations, deletions, or both. Loss of Rb function eliminates the G1/S checkpoint by releasing E2F transcription factors, enabling uncontrolled S-phase entry.

biological_processes: negative regulation of G1/S transition of mitotic cell cycle

evidence.reference_title: Retinoblastoma Expression and Targeting by CDK4/6 Inhibitors in Small Cell Lung Cancer.
evidence.snippet: The canonical model of "small cell lung cancer" (SCLC) depicts tumors arising from dual inactivation of TP53 and RB1.

nodes.description: TP53 is inactivated in >90% of SCLC through mutations, deletions, or both. Loss of p53 function eliminates the G1/S checkpoint and apoptotic response to DNA damage, enabling survival despite genomic instability.

biological_processes: DNA damage response, signal transduction by p53 class mediator
